principle.name: MID-SHAFT CONTACT CREATES A TEMPORARY TOOL PIVOT
principle.statement: When a long rigid tool is struck or blocked away from its tip, the acquired contact can become a temporary pivot. The body may continue to compress behind that constraint while the far tip overshoots, so release and recovery must repay two-sided tool debt rather than reverse the incoming sweep.
principle.novelty_vs_prior_v2: Contact point lies inside the tool span and visibly re-pivots both tool ends; this is neither axial thrust recovery, tool-tool bind, environmental hammer rebound, hooked deflection, rear-clearance sidestep, nor elbow crush.
